notes:
[French—“to the purpose”]
A comment is *à propos* (or *apropos*) if it is exactly appropriate for the situation.

definition: for a particular purpose; only for the matter at hand
notes:
[Latin—“for this”]
An *ad hoc* committee is a committee established for a particular purpose or to deal with a particular problem.

pron: uh fish yuh NAH doh, ah fee syow NAH doh
notes:
[Spanish—“affectionate one”]
An *aficionado* of football is a football fan. An *aficionado* of theater is a theater fan.

[Italian—“in the fresh”]
An *al fresco* meal is a picnic.

example: Recent articles have described Mr. Petroleum as “an energy company *apparatchik*” and Mayor Atlanta as “a Democratic Party *apparatchik* turned popular leader.”

notes:
[French—“in the current”]
To be *au courant* is to know all the latest information.

example: A *bona fide* linguistic expert, Alli speaks forty languages, including six Aboriginal tongues.
notes:
[Latin—“in/with good faith”]
The noun form is *bona fides* (singular), meaning proof of credentials or of sincerity.

definition: the power to do whatever one wants
notes:
[French—“blank card”]
To give someone *carte blanche* is to give that person the license to do anything.

[Latin—“from the fact”]
Your *de facto* boss is the person who tells you what to do. Your *de jure* (dee JYUR) boss is the person who is technically in charge of you. *De jure* (“from the law”) means according to rule of law.

pron: duh ri GUR, duh ree GUER
definition: obligatory; required by fashion or custom
notes:
[French—“indispensable”]
Long hair for men was *de rigueur* in the late 1960s. Evening wear is *de rigueur* at a formal party.

definition: an illusory feeling of having seen or done something before
notes:
[French—“already seen”]
To have *déjà vu* is to believe that one has already done or seen what one is in fact doing or seeing for the first time.

example: Masha thinks *ennui* is sophisticated, but her jaded remarks bore me to tears.

pron: fet uh kohm PLEE, fayt ah kahm PLEE
definition: something that is already done and that cannot be undone
example: Our committee spent a long time debating whether to have the building painted, but the project was a *fait accompli;* the chairman had already hired someone to do it.
Henry committed a *faux pas* when he told the hostess that her party had been boring.

notes:
[French—“fixed idea”]
An *idée fixe* is an idea that obsesses you or that you can’t get out of your mind.

definition: by or because of that very fact
example: Under the discriminatory employment policy, people with children are *ipso facto* ineligible for promotion.

definition: deep and usually contagious enjoyment of life
example: Antonio’s *joie de vivre* made his office a pleasant place to work for everyone connected with it.

definition: a small group that rules a country after its government is overthrown
example: After the rebels had driven out the president, the Latin American country was ruled by a *junta* of army officers.

pron: les ay FAIR, lay zay FAIR
definition: a doctrine of noninterference by government in the economy; noninterference in general
notes:
[French—“let do”]
To believe in *laissez-faire* is to believe the government should exert no control over business. It’s also possible to adopt a *laissez-faire* attitude about other matters.

pron: may ah KOOL pah, may uh KUL puh
example: *Mea culpa, mea culpa*. I was the one who put the dog in the cat’s bed.

pron: noh loh kahn TEN duh ree
notes:
[Latin—“I do not wish to contend”]
A plea in a court case that is the equivalent of a guilty plea, but it doesn’t include an actual admission of guilt.

definition: a statement that does not follow logically from what has gone before
example: Bill’s saying “Forty-three degrees” when Lola asked “May I have the butter?” was a *non sequitur*.

pron: per SOH nuh nahn GRAH tuh
example: Fernando’s altercation with the principal made him *persona non grata* in the Parent-Teacher Association.
notes:
[Latin—“unacceptable person”]
In diplomacy, *persona non grata* often refers to an emissary blacklisted (for suspected espionage or crime, or for political reasons) by a host country.

definition: something given or done in return for something else
example: The politician said he would do what we had asked him to do, but there was a *quid pro quo:* He said we had to bribe him first.

pron: ray zohn DET, ray zohn DET ruh
example: Money was the greedy rich man’s *raison d’être*.

pron: RAHN day voo, RAHN duh voo
example: The young couple met behind the bleachers for a discreet *rendezvous*.

pron: sin ay kwoh NOHN, sye nee kway NAHN
example: Understanding is the *sine qua non* of a successful marriage.

pron: stayt us KWOH, stat us KWOH
notes:
[Latin—“state in which”]
The *status quo* is the way things are now.

definition: unique; in a class of one’s own
notes:
[Latin—“of one’s own kind”]
To be *sui generis* is to be unlike anyone else.

pron: tayt uh TAYT, tet ah TET
definition: a private conversation between two people
example: The two attorneys resolved their differences in a brief *tête-à-tête* before the trial began.
The students’ relationship *vis-à-vis* the administration was one of confrontation.
Nudnik was always out of step with the *zeitgeist;* he had short hair in 1970 and long hair in 1980.
